results.label: this tree ships the zone-method vocabulary and the consolidation walk (src/bots/smc.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the committed parent really does have only one geometry and no way to ask for another (the control is non-vacuous)
real analyses were built for both methods (the comparison is not vacuous)
with no method chosen, every candidate the model builds is byte-identical to the committed parent’s
and no new candidate key appears at all: the choice is not a hidden field on a setup
the filter block names the method on every read, so the geometry is never anonymous
and the range read names itself as range, with the number of zones actually plotted that way
over every analysed zone the two methods pair up by origin, and the range box contains the pivot box
and the range method really does catch a return the pivot method never sees (price came back into the consolidation without touching the candle)
the wider zone moves the stop on the setups it is used on: the distance from entry to stop is never smaller
and the model says so where the trader chooses it: the filter publishes the trade-off rather than a winner
a method the app cannot plot runs the pivot geometry and the filter carries the request AND the sentence
an unreadable read (the short-series sentinel) names the method that WOULD be used and reports that nothing ran
the two reads disagree about zones and levels only because the boxes differ: the verdict and filter blocks keep the same shape

scope: M30 engine: the two zone methods at the decision surface, against the committed parent: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
